claims.text: The target alloy is an equiatomic Co-free Fe-Ni-Cr-Mn alloy derived by removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
The dynamic strength-ductility balance of Co-free FeNiCrMn arises primarily from temperature- and strain-rate-dependent dynamic strain aging.
Mobile solute atoms can form transient Cottrell-type atmospheres that intermittently pin or lock moving dislocations.
Dynamic locking and breakaway of dislocations by mobile solutes produces serrated flow.
Dynamic strain aging causes variations or fluctuations in yield strength.
At intermediate temperatures and strain rates, solute mobility becomes sufficient for solutes to attach intermittently to moving dislocations.
At temperatures too low for solute mobility, dynamic strain-aging effects and serrations diminish.
At ultra-high strain rates, dislocations move too rapidly for effective solute pinning, so dynamic strain-aging effects and serrations diminish.
Transient grain refinement and associated grain-boundary sliding may contribute when dislocation-mediated plasticity becomes less active.
At approximately 300 K and 1 s^-1, the Co-free alloy exhibits uniform plastic flow, a standard strength-ductility balance, and little or no serration.
Relative to the 300 K, 1 s^-1 baseline, conditions favorable to dynamic strain aging will increase flow-serration amplitude.
Relative to the baseline, conditions favorable to dynamic strain aging will enhance yield-strength fluctuations.
The proposed mechanism is applicable roughly from 200 K to 700 K and from 10^-3 s^-1 to a few thousand s^-1.
Outside the proposed regime, thermal activation or inertial effects dominate over dynamic strain aging.
A controlled comparison of Co-free FeNiCrMn with CoCrFeMnNi across matched temperatures and strain rates can test whether serrations track solute-atmosphere formation and dislocation locking.
Failure of serrated flow to vary with temperature and strain rate as predicted would falsify dynamic strain aging as the primary explanation.
Absence of a correlation between transient solute atmospheres or dislocation locking and the anomalous mechanical response would falsify dynamic strain aging as the primary explanation.

contradictions.description: The baseline of 300 K and 1 s^-1 appears to fall within the vaguely defined intermediate temperature and strain-rate regime where dynamic strain aging and enhanced serration are predicted, yet the baseline is asserted to show little or no serration.

The boundary defines the full 200–700 K and 10^-3 to several-thousand s^-1 range as applicable to the mechanism, while the mechanism states that the cold and ultra-high-rate extremes within that range suppress solute pinning and serrations.
